title: Early Identification of Peripheral Ischemic Complications in ECMO Patients via Infrared Thermography
summary:
In very severe heart or lung failure, ECMO can oxygenate the blood outside the body and support circulation. Large tubes, called cannulas, are usually inserted through the blood vessels in the groin. These cannulas can obstruct blood flow to the leg. If a leg does not receive enough blood, serious consequences can follow, including surgery or amputation. Because patients are usually in an induced coma, they cannot report symptoms, and a circulation problem is sometimes recognised late.

Poorly perfused skin is cooler than well-perfused skin. A thermal camera can measure this without contact, without pain and without radiation. In this study, we take thermal images of both legs and the upper body once a day and compare the temperatures. We want to find out whether reduced blood flow can be detected reliably and as early as possible in this way. Participants undergo no additional procedures and face no risks.
conditions: Other specified complications of cardiac and vascular prosthetic devices, implants and grafts

interventions.name: Patients receiving extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) in the intensive care units of University Hospital Oldenburg.
